title: Counting on to add
keyIdea: To add, you do not need to count everything from one. Say the first number and keep it in your head. Then count on one more for each thing you add: 5 … 6, 7. Start from the bigger number, because it means fewer counts, and the total is the same.
familyTip: Put 5 toys in a box and close the lid. Say five and tap the lid. Then add 2 more toys, one at a time, and say six, seven together. If your child opens the box to count from one, close the lid and say the box number again.

visual.caption: Which number do you start from? Drag each sum to its bigger number, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: hide cars in a jar and count on, jump a frog along a number track, start from the bigger number, fill a bus, and keep count on your fingers.

kid: There are 5 cars in a jar. You cannot see them. You do not need to. The jar says 5, so you know there are 5.
Two more cars come. Say five in your head. Then count on: six, seven. Now there are 7 cars.
Do not say five again for the first new car. The first new car is six.
Got 2 and 6? Start from 6, the bigger one. Six … seven, eight. That is quick! And 2 and 6 is 8, the same as 6 and 2.
adult: Ages 4 to 5. Counting on is the step after counting all. The child holds the first number (the cardinal value of the first group) and counts on from it, rather than counting both groups from one. It builds on the Reception idea of one more than a number (Development Matters 2021) and leads to the Year 1 National Curriculum goal of adding one-digit numbers. Research on how children add (Carpenter and Moser, 1984; Fuson, 1982) shows the usual path: count all, then count on from the first number, then count on from the larger number. Key words: count on, number track, total, add, more, the larger number first (commutativity).

Hide the first group, in a jar, a box or under a cloth, so the child cannot count it again. Say its number aloud and tap it. Then count on for each new object, one number per object. A number track (squares labelled 1 to 10) works the same way: stand on the first number and count the jumps.

Common mistakes: saying the first number again for the first new object (5, 6 for adding 2, so the total is one short); counting the starting square on a track as a jump; starting from the smaller number and counting many times; thinking 2 + 6 and 6 + 2 give different totals; and losing track of how many have been counted on. Fingers fix the last one: one finger up for each number said. Be careful that counting on is only used for adding small numbers, about 1 to 4; for bigger ones, use number bonds and doubles.

In the lab your child counts on from a hidden jar of cars, jumps a frog along a number track, chooses the bigger number to start from, says how many are on a bus when more get on, and keeps track with fingers.

practice.prompt: There are {n} cars in a jar. {k} more cars come. How many cars are there now?
practice.hint: Say {n} in your head. Then count on one more for each new car.
practice.explain: Start at {n} and count on {k} more. {n} and {k} more is {=n+k}, so there are {=n+k} cars.

practice.prompt: A frog is on {n} on a number track. It jumps {k} times, one square each time. Which number does it land on?
practice.hint: Do not count the square it starts on. Count the jumps.
practice.explain: Each jump goes to the next number. From {n}, {k} jumps lands on {=n+k}.

practice.prompt: You add 2 and 7. Which number is quicker to start from?
practice.hint: Start from the bigger number, then count on the smaller one.
practice.explain: Start from 7 and count on 2: eight, nine. That is only 2 counts.

practice.prompt: Sam has 6 in his head. He adds 2. He says: six, seven. What went wrong?
choices: He said six again; it should be seven, eight
practice.hint: Six is already in his head. What is one more than six?
practice.explain: The first new one is seven, so he should say seven, eight. 6 and 2 is 8.

practice.prompt: Is 3 and 5 the same as 5 and 3?
practice.hint: Try both on your fingers: start from 5 and count on 3.
practice.explain: The order does not change the total. Both make 8, so you can start from the bigger one.

choices: Start from the first number and count the new ones
pool.hint: Do you need to count the first group again?
pool.explain: Counting on means you keep the first number in your head and count on from it.

pool.prompt: {n} people are on a bus. {k} more get on. How many are on the bus now?
pool.hint: Hold {n} in your head. The first person to get on is one more than {n}.
pool.explain: Count on {k} from {n}. {n} and {k} is {=n+k}, so {=n+k} people are on the bus.

pool.prompt: 5 cars are in a jar. 3 more come. What do you say?
pool.hint: Say the jar number, then one new number for each car.
pool.explain: Five is in the jar. Then six, seven, eight for the 3 new cars. 5 and 3 is 8.

pool.prompt: A frog is on 3. It jumps 4 times. Where does it land?
pool.hint: Count the jumps: 4, 5, 6, 7. Do not count the square it starts on.
pool.explain: From 3, the jumps land on 4, 5, 6 and 7. So 3 and 4 is 7.

pool.prompt: You hold {n} in your head and put up {k} fingers as you count on. What number do you stop on?
pool.hint: Say one number for each finger, starting with one more than {n}.
pool.explain: One finger for each number after {n}. With {k} fingers up you stop on {=n+k}.

pool.prompt: To add 1 and 8, which is quicker?
pool.explain: From 8 you count just one: nine. From 1 you would count eight times. Both give 9.

pool.prompt: You add 2 to 6. How many fingers do you put up?
pool.hint: The 6 is in your head. Fingers show only what you add.
pool.explain: Put up 2 fingers, one for seven and one for eight. 6 and 2 is 8.

pool.prompt: Mia says 4 and 5 is 8. She said four, five, six, seven, eight. What was her slip?
choices: She said four again; start the count at five
pool.hint: Hold 4 in your head. Which number comes first when you count on?
pool.explain: Start from 5 (the bigger one): six, seven, eight, nine. 4 and 5 is 9, not 8.

pool.prompt: Why hide the first group in a jar?
choices: So you say its number and do not count it again
pool.hint: What do you do instead of counting the hidden cars?
pool.explain: You say the jar number and keep it in your head, then count on. It stops you counting from one.
